intro: Welcome! Today you write the short messages you send every day: a WhatsApp message or an email to a friend with your news and a question, and a polite message to your boss. At the end you write a short story about your weekend in 35–50 words, using the past you already know.
teachingNotes: Build on a1-writing-about-me: capitals, full stops, a comma after the greeting (Hi Sari, / Dear Pak Hasan,) and after the ending word (Love, / Best wishes,), and endings like See you soon! and Write soon!. A short informal message now has four parts: greeting (Hi Sari!) → news (Guess what? I got a new job!) → a question back (How are you? How was your trip?) → ending + name (See you soon, Rina). Teach 'Guess what?' as a fixed phrase that introduces news.

Friend or boss (register): with friends, Hi/Hey, Thanks!, btw (= by the way), one or two emoji, Love, / See you soon, / Take care, are all fine. With a boss, teacher or client: Dear + title + name (Dear Pak Hasan, / Dear Bu Ani, / Dear Mr Brown,), Thank you very much, 'By the way' written out, no emoji and no chat abbreviations (thx, pls, btw), and Best wishes, / Kind regards, before the name. Indonesian traps: dropping Pak/Bu and writing the boss's first name only (*'Hey Hasan!'), 'Bye bye' to end a work email, and Indonesian chat habits like everything in small letters. 'Mr Brown' (British) = 'Mr. Brown' (American): both correct.

News in the past: Indonesian only adds a time word (Kemarin aku lulus ujian / Td aku beli motor), so the #1 error is *'Yesterday I pass my driving test' or *'Last week we move to a new flat': whenever there is yesterday, last … or … ago, check the verb is past (passed, moved, bought, got, had). Also watch *'I was buy a motorbike' (was is not a past marker for other verbs). Native speakers often give news with the present perfect (I've got a new job), but the learner hasn't met it: the past simple (I got a new job!) is natural and correct; accept a correct present perfect but don't teach it.

Asking questions back: How are you? / And you? / How about you? / How was your weekend? (was + adjective in the answer) / Did you + base verb …? / What did you + base verb …? Watch *'Did you went…?', *'Where you went?' and *'Were you go…?'. From a2-making-plans and a2-will the learner may end with a plan or an invitation (Would you like to meet on Sunday? I'll call you tomorrow. I'm going to visit you next month.): accept them; a reaction to a friend's news (Congratulations! That's great! Oh no, I'm sorry!) is a useful fixed phrase.

Short story (35–50 words, counted between spaces; I'm = one word): start with when, where and who (Last Saturday I went to Bandung with my sister.), give 2–3 events in order with time words (in the morning, at seven, in the afternoon, in the evening, at one o'clock), and finish with how it was (we were tired but happy). Past simple all the way through: the common error is switching back to the present in the middle (*'We went to the beach. We swim in the sea.'). Join ideas with and, but and because (A1). Don't teach first/then/next/finally, before/after/when as linkers or 'so' for a result: they come in a2-linkers-sequence, which is not in this path; if the learner uses them correctly, accept them.

Limits: no present perfect, past continuous, could or comparatives (not in this path). Don't teach formal letters (Dear Sir or Madam, Yours faithfully). Typed answers are lowercased when checked, so capitals can't be graded in the checkpoint: give feedback on capitals and full stops in the free practice (the story and the full message) instead.

keyPoints.title: A short informal message, and when to be formal
keyPoints.explanation: A short message to a friend has four parts: a greeting (Hi Sari!), your news, a question back, and an ending with your name (See you soon, Rina). With friends, Thanks!, btw and emoji are fine. With a boss or a teacher, write Dear + Pak/Bu/Mr + name, Thank you very much, no emoji or chat short forms, and end with Best wishes, or Kind regards,.

examples.id: Salam, Rina (penutup sopan untuk atasan atau klien)

id.title: Pesan informal yang singkat, dan kapan harus formal
id.explanation: Pesan singkat untuk teman punya empat bagian: salam pembuka (Hi Sari!), kabarmu, pertanyaan balik, dan penutup dengan namamu (See you soon, Rina). Dengan teman, Thanks!, btw dan emoji boleh. Dengan atasan atau guru, tulis Dear + Pak/Bu/Mr + nama, Thank you very much, tanpa emoji atau singkatan chat, dan tutup dengan Best wishes, atau Kind regards,.

keyPoints.title: Simple news in the past, and a question back
keyPoints.explanation: Give news with the past simple: Guess what? I got a new job! / We moved to Depok last week. The time word alone is not enough (not 'Yesterday I pass'). Then ask your friend something: How are you? How was your trip? Did you + base verb? What did you + base verb?

examples.en: Guess what? I got a new job!
examples.id: Coba tebak! Aku dapat kerja baru!

examples.en: How was your trip to Bali?
Did you see Dimas at the party?

id.title: Kabar sederhana di masa lalu, dan pertanyaan balik
id.explanation: Sampaikan kabar dengan past simple: Guess what? I got a new job! / We moved to Depok last week. Kata waktu saja tidak cukup (bukan 'Yesterday I pass'). Lalu tanyakan sesuatu ke temanmu: How are you? How was your trip? Did you + kata kerja dasar? What did you + kata kerja dasar?

keyPoints.title: A short story of 35–50 words
keyPoints.explanation: Start with when, where and who. Then tell 2–3 things that happened, in order, with time words (in the morning, at seven, in the evening). End with how it was. Use the past for every verb, and join ideas with and, but and because. Count every word between spaces.

examples.en: Last Saturday I went to Bandung with my sister.
examples.id: Sabtu lalu aku pergi ke Bandung bersama kakak perempuanku.

examples.en: In the afternoon we visited a tea garden.

id.title: Cerita pendek 35–50 kata
id.explanation: Mulai dengan kapan, di mana dan dengan siapa. Lalu ceritakan 2–3 kejadian, berurutan, dengan kata waktu (in the morning, at seven, in the evening). Akhiri dengan bagaimana rasanya. Pakai bentuk lampau untuk setiap kata kerja, dan gabungkan ide dengan and, but dan because. Hitung setiap kata yang dipisah spasi.

guidedPractice.prompt: You're writing a WhatsApp message to your best friend Nadia. Write a friendly ending phrase to put before your name.
guidedPractice.hint: For friends: See you soon, / Love, / Take care, — then your name.

guidedPractice.prompt: Use the notes to write your news in one sentence: my sister / have / a baby girl / last night
expected: my sister had a baby girl last night
last night my sister had a baby girl
guidedPractice.hint: last night = the past, and have is irregular: have → had.

guidedPractice.prompt: Budi wrote: 'I went to a concert on Saturday!' Ask him a question back. Use the notes: how / be / it
guidedPractice.hint: The concert is in the past, so be → was: How ___ it?

guidedPractice.prompt: This sentence is from a story about last week. Write it in the past: In the morning I take an ojek to the station.
expected: in the morning i took an ojek to the station
i took an ojek to the station in the morning

guidedPractice.prompt: Join the two sentences with but: The hotel was small. It was very clean.
expected: the hotel was small but it was very clean
the hotel was small but very clean
guidedPractice.hint: but joins two ideas that are different (small ↔ clean).

independentPractice.prompt: Write a short WhatsApp message to your friend Sari: a greeting, your news (you got a new job), a question for her, and an ending with your name.
expected: hi sari guess what i got a new job how are you see you soon rina
independentPractice.hint: Hi Sari! → Guess what? I got … → How are you? → See you soon, + your name.

independentPractice.prompt: Write one question to ask a friend about their weekend.
expected: what did you do at the weekend
what did you do on the weekend
did you have a good weekend
independentPractice.hint: How was …? or What did you do …? (did + do, not did + did).

independentPractice.prompt: Write a short story (35–50 words) about last weekend. Say when, where and who; tell 2–3 things in order with time words; say how it was. Use the past, and join ideas with and, but or because.
expected: last saturday i went to bandung with my sister we took the train at seven in the morning in the afternoon we visited a tea garden and had lunch at a small warung it rained in the evening but we were happy because the food was great
independentPractice.hint: Check every verb: went, took, visited, had, was/were. Then count the words: 35–50.

assessment.prompt: You're writing an email to your manager, Bu Ani. Write a polite ending phrase to put before your name.
acceptableAnswers: best wishes
kind regards
best regards
regards
warm regards
yours sincerely
assessment.rubric: Correct: Best wishes, / Kind regards, / Best regards, (comma optional when typed). Friendly endings (Love, See you soon, Take care, Bye bye, xx) = 0: too informal for a manager. Only a name = 0.

assessment.prompt: Your manager, Pak Hasan, helped you with a report. Write a polite thank-you for your email to him (not 'Thanks!').
acceptableAnswers: thank you very much
thank you so much
thank you for your help
thank you very much for your help
thank you so much for your help
thank you for your help with the report
thank you very much for your help with the report
thank you for helping me
thank you very much for helping me
thank you pak hasan
thank you very much pak hasan
thank you for your help pak hasan
assessment.rubric: Correct: Thank you very much (for your help). Plain 'Thank you' = 80. 'Thanks!', 'Thx' or an emoji = 20: fine for a friend, too casual for a manager. 'Thank you for your helping' = 60.

assessment.prompt: Use the notes to write your news in one sentence: I / buy / a new motorbike / last week
acceptableAnswers: i bought a new motorbike last week
last week i bought a new motorbike
i bought a new motorcycle last week
last week i bought a new motorcycle
assessment.rubric: Correct: I bought a new motorbike last week. 'buy' or 'buyed' = 30 (buy is irregular: bought). 'I was buy' = 20. 'brought' instead of 'bought' = 60 (a different verb: bring).

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake in this news: Guess what? Last week we move to a new flat!
acceptableAnswers: guess what last week we moved to a new flat
last week we moved to a new flat
we moved to a new flat last week
guess what we moved to a new flat last week
last week we moved to a new apartment
guess what last week we moved to a new apartment
assessment.rubric: Correct: Last week we moved to a new flat. 'moving' or 'are moving' = 20. 'moveed' = 70 (move ends in -e, so just + d). Changing 'last week' instead of the verb = 0.

assessment.prompt: Sari wrote: 'I was in Lombok last week!' Ask her a question back about the food. Use the notes: what / you / eat
acceptableAnswers: what did you eat
what did you eat there
what did you eat in lombok
assessment.rubric: Correct: What did you eat (there)? 'What did you ate?' = 50 (after did, the base verb). 'What you ate?' or 'What you eat?' = 30 (did is missing). 'What were you eat?' = 20.

assessment.prompt: This sentence is from a story about last weekend. Write it in the past: On Sunday we go to the market and buy some fruit.
acceptableAnswers: on sunday we went to the market and bought some fruit
we went to the market on sunday and bought some fruit
on sunday we went to the market and we bought some fruit
assessment.rubric: Correct: On Sunday we went to the market and bought some fruit. Only one verb changed = 50. 'goed' or 'buyed' = minus 30 each. 'brought' instead of 'bought' = minus 20.

assessment.prompt: Join the two sentences with because: We were very tired. We walked for five hours.
acceptableAnswers: we were very tired because we walked for five hours
we were very tired because we walked for 5 hours
assessment.rubric: Correct: We were very tired because we walked for five hours. 'We walked for five hours because we were very tired' (reason and result swapped) = 20. 'because' with 'walk' (present) = 50.

material.title: Four parts of a short message

blocks.text:
A WhatsApp message or a short email to a friend usually has **four parts**:

- a **greeting**: *Hi Sari!* or *Hi Sari,* (Hi + name, then ! or a comma)
- your **news**: something that happened, in the **past**: *Guess what? I passed my driving test yesterday!*
- a **question back**, because a message is a conversation: *How are you? How was your trip?*
- an **ending** and your **name**: *See you soon, Rina* / *Love, Rina* / *Take care, Rina*

**Guess what?** (= coba tebak!) is a fixed friendly phrase to start your news. It's a question, so it has a question mark.

id.text:
Pesan WhatsApp atau email singkat untuk teman biasanya punya **empat bagian**:

- **salam pembuka**: *Hi Sari!* atau *Hi Sari,* (Hi + nama, lalu ! atau koma)
- **kabarmu**: sesuatu yang sudah terjadi, dalam bentuk **lampau**: *Guess what? I passed my driving test yesterday!*
- **pertanyaan balik**, karena pesan itu seperti percakapan: *How are you? How was your trip?*
- **penutup** dan **namamu**: *See you soon, Rina* / *Love, Rina* / *Take care, Rina*

**Guess what?** (= coba tebak!) adalah ungkapan tetap yang ramah untuk memulai kabar. Bentuknya pertanyaan, jadi pakai tanda tanya.

rows.en: Guess what? I passed my driving test yesterday! I was very nervous, but it was OK.
rows.id: Coba tebak! Aku lulus ujian SIM kemarin! Aku gugup banget, tapi lancar kok.

rows.en: How are you? How was your trip to Bali?
rows.id: Apa kabar? Gimana liburanmu ke Bali?

blocks.text: **Same rules as in your A1 messages.** A capital for the first word, for **I** and for names (*Sari, Bali*); a full stop, ! or ? at the end of each sentence; a comma before your name in the ending (*See you soon, Rina*). In chat many people type *i passed my test!!!* in small letters. With a new friend or in an email, write it properly: it's easier to read and looks friendly, not careless. And one ! is enough.

id.text: **Aturannya sama seperti pesan A1-mu.** Huruf kapital untuk kata pertama, untuk **I** dan untuk nama (*Sari, Bali*); titik, ! atau ? di akhir setiap kalimat; koma sebelum namamu di penutup (*See you soon, Rina*). Di chat banyak orang mengetik *i passed my test!!!* dengan huruf kecil semua. Untuk teman baru atau di email, tulis dengan rapi: lebih mudah dibaca dan terlihat ramah, bukan asal-asalan. Dan satu ! sudah cukup.

blocks.prompt: Which part is missing? Hi Dimas! I bought a new laptop yesterday. See you soon, Budi
blocks.explain: Hi Dimas! is the greeting, I bought a new laptop yesterday is the news, and See you soon, Budi is the ending. There is no question for Dimas, like How are you? or How was your weekend?

id.prompt: Bagian mana yang tidak ada? Hi Dimas! I bought a new laptop yesterday. See you soon, Budi
id.explain: Hi Dimas! adalah salam pembuka, I bought a new laptop yesterday adalah kabarnya, dan See you soon, Budi adalah penutup. Tidak ada pertanyaan untuk Dimas, seperti How are you? atau How was your weekend?

material.title: To a friend or to your boss?

blocks.text:
The same message sounds different to a **friend** and to your **boss**, a teacher or a client. With friends you can be **informal** (santai): *Hi*, *Thanks!*, *btw* (= by the way, ngomong-ngomong) and an emoji or two 😊. With a boss you are **formal** (resmi, sopan): write words in full, no emoji.

- greeting: *Hi Sari!* → **Dear Pak Hasan,** / **Dear Mr Brown,**
- thanks: *Thanks!* → **Thank you very much.**
- by the way: *btw* → **By the way,**
- ending: *See you soon, / Love, / Take care,* → **Best wishes,** / **Kind regards,**

id.text:
Pesan yang sama terdengar berbeda untuk **teman** dan untuk **atasanmu**, guru atau klien. Dengan teman kamu boleh **informal** (santai): *Hi*, *Thanks!*, *btw* (= by the way, ngomong-ngomong) dan satu-dua emoji 😊. Dengan atasan kamu **formal** (resmi, sopan): tulis kata-katanya lengkap, tanpa emoji.

- salam pembuka: *Hi Sari!* → **Dear Pak Hasan,** / **Dear Mr Brown,**
- terima kasih: *Thanks!* → **Thank you very much.**
- ngomong-ngomong: *btw* → **By the way,**
- penutup: *See you soon, / Love, / Take care,* → **Best wishes,** / **Kind regards,**

rows.en: Hi Dimas! Thanks for the photos! btw, are you free on Saturday?
rows.id: Hai Dimas! Makasih fotonya! Btw, kamu kosong hari Sabtu?

rows.en: Dear Pak Hasan, Thank you very much for the meeting today.
rows.id: Yth. Pak Hasan, Terima kasih banyak untuk rapat hari ini.
rows.note: to a boss: formal, Pak stays

id.note: untuk atasan: formal, Pak tetap ditulis

rows.en: By the way, the meeting room is ready.
rows.id: Oh ya, ruang rapatnya sudah siap.
rows.note: by the way written in full

blocks.text: **Indonesian traps.** At work in Indonesia you say *Pak Hasan* or *Bu Ani*: keep **Pak/Bu** in English too (*Dear Pak Hasan,*). Don't write only the first name (*Hey Hasan!*), and don't end a work email with *Bye bye*: it's too casual. Short forms from Indonesian chat (*makasih, wkwk*) and English ones (*thx, pls, btw*) are for friends only. **Mr Brown** is British; American English writes **Mr. Brown** with a full stop. Both are correct.

id.text: **Jebakan dari kebiasaan Indonesia.** Di kantor di Indonesia kamu bilang *Pak Hasan* atau *Bu Ani*: pertahankan **Pak/Bu** juga dalam bahasa Inggris (*Dear Pak Hasan,*). Jangan tulis nama depannya saja (*Hey Hasan!*), dan jangan menutup email kerja dengan *Bye bye*: terlalu santai. Singkatan chat Indonesia (*makasih, wkwk*) dan Inggris (*thx, pls, btw*) hanya untuk teman. **Mr Brown** itu British; bahasa Inggris Amerika menulis **Mr.** dengan titik. Keduanya benar.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence is right for an email to your boss?
options: By the way, the report is ready.
blocks.explain: To a boss you write words in full, with a capital letter and a full stop, and without emoji. btw, thx and 👍 are fine with friends, but too casual for work.

id.prompt: Kalimat mana yang tepat untuk email ke atasanmu?
id.explain: Untuk atasan, tulis kata-katanya lengkap, dengan huruf kapital dan titik, tanpa emoji. btw, thx dan 👍 boleh untuk teman, tapi terlalu santai untuk urusan kerja.

material.title: Your news in the past, and a question back

blocks.text:
News is usually something that **already happened**, so the verb is in the **past simple**: *I **got** a new job! We **moved** to Depok last week. My sister **had** a baby!* Regular verbs take **-ed** (*passed, moved*); the common irregular ones have their own form (*got, had, bought, went, saw*).

Then **ask back**. A message with only your news sounds like you don't care about your friend.

- *How are you?* / *And you?* / *How about you?*
- *How was your weekend / your trip?* (was = the past of is)
- **Did you** + base verb (kata kerja dasar)? *Did you see the match?*
- **What did you** + base verb? *What did you buy?*

When a friend gives you news, react first: *Congratulations!* (selamat!) / *That's great!* / *Oh no, I'm sorry!*

id.text:
Kabar biasanya tentang sesuatu yang **sudah terjadi**, jadi kata kerjanya memakai **past simple**: *I **got** a new job! We **moved** to Depok last week. My sister **had** a baby!* Kata kerja beraturan ditambah **-ed** (*passed, moved*); yang tidak beraturan punya bentuk sendiri (*got, had, bought, went, saw*).

Lalu **tanya balik**. Pesan yang isinya hanya kabarmu terdengar seperti kamu tidak peduli pada temanmu.

- *How are you?* / *And you?* / *How about you?*
- *How was your weekend / your trip?* (was = bentuk lampau dari is)
- **Did you** + kata kerja dasar? *Did you see the match?*
- **What did you** + kata kerja dasar? *What did you buy?*

Saat teman memberi kabar, tanggapi dulu: *Congratulations!* (selamat!) / *That's great!* / *Oh no, I'm sorry!*

rows.en: Guess what? We moved to Depok last week!
rows.id: Coba tebak! Kami pindah ke Depok minggu lalu!

rows.en: Dimas and Ayu had a baby boy on Friday!
rows.id: Dimas dan Ayu punya bayi laki-laki hari Jumat!

rows.en: Did you go to Dewi's wedding?

rows.id: Selamat ya! Kabar yang bagus banget!

blocks.text: **The time word isn't enough.** In Indonesian chat you write *Kemarin aku lulus ujian* or *Td aku beli motor*: the verb never changes, only *kemarin* or *tadi* shows the past. In English the verb must change too: *Yesterday I **passed** my test*, not *Yesterday I pass*. And *was* is not a past marker: *I bought a motorbike*, not *I was buy*. In questions, **did** already shows the past, so the verb goes back to its base: *Did you **see** it?*, not *Did you saw it?*

id.text: **Kata waktu saja tidak cukup.** Di chat bahasa Indonesia kamu menulis *Kemarin aku lulus ujian* atau *Td aku beli motor*: kata kerjanya tidak berubah, hanya *kemarin* atau *tadi* yang menunjukkan masa lalu. Dalam bahasa Inggris kata kerjanya juga harus berubah: *Yesterday I **passed** my test*, bukan *Yesterday I pass*. Dan *was* bukan penanda lampau untuk kata kerja lain: *I bought a motorbike*, bukan *I was buy*. Dalam pertanyaan, **did** sudah menunjukkan masa lalu, jadi kata kerjanya kembali ke bentuk dasar: *Did you **see** it?*, bukan *Did you saw it?*

blocks.prompt: Sari wrote: 'I went to Yogyakarta last week!' Which question can you ask back?
blocks.explain: Questions in the past: Did + you + base verb, so Did you go…? 'Did you went' shows the past twice, and 'were' can't go with another verb like go.

id.prompt: Sari menulis: 'I went to Yogyakarta last week!' Pertanyaan mana yang bisa kamu kirim balik?
id.explain: Pertanyaan lampau: Did + you + kata kerja dasar, jadi Did you go…? 'Did you went' menunjukkan masa lalu dua kali, dan 'were' tidak bisa dipakai bersama kata kerja lain seperti go.

id.title: Kabarmu di masa lalu, dan pertanyaan balik

blocks.text:
A short story about your weekend, a trip or a funny day needs only **3–5 sentences** (35–50 words). A simple plan:

- **Start**: when, where and who: *Last Saturday I went to Bandung with my sister.*
- **Middle**: 2–3 things that happened, **in order**. Time words show the order: *in the morning, at seven, in the afternoon, in the evening, at one o'clock*.
- **End**: how it was or how you felt: *We were tired but happy.*

Use the **past for every verb**, from the first sentence to the last. Join ideas with **and** (dan), **but** (tapi) and **because** (karena). To count, count everything between spaces: *o'clock* is one word.

id.text:
Cerita pendek tentang akhir pekanmu, perjalanan atau hari yang lucu cukup **3–5 kalimat** (35–50 kata). Rencana sederhananya:

- **Awal**: kapan, di mana dan dengan siapa: *Last Saturday I went to Bandung with my sister.*
- **Tengah**: 2–3 kejadian, **berurutan**. Kata waktu menunjukkan urutannya: *in the morning, at seven, in the afternoon, in the evening, at one o'clock*.
- **Akhir**: bagaimana rasanya: *We were tired but happy.*

Pakai **bentuk lampau untuk setiap kata kerja**, dari kalimat pertama sampai terakhir. Gabungkan ide dengan **and** (dan), **but** (tapi) dan **because** (karena). Untuk menghitung, hitung semua yang dipisah spasi: *o'clock* dihitung satu kata.

rows.en: Last Saturday I went to Bandung with my sister.
rows.id: Sabtu lalu aku pergi ke Bandung bersama kakak perempuanku.

id.note: awal: kapan, di mana, dengan siapa

rows.en: We took the train at seven in the morning.
rows.id: Kami naik kereta jam tujuh pagi.

rows.en: In the afternoon we visited a tea garden and had lunch at a small warung.
rows.id: Sorenya kami mengunjungi kebun teh dan makan siang di warung kecil.
rows.note: a time word shows the order

rows.en: It rained in the evening, but we were happy because the food was great.
rows.id: Malamnya hujan, tapi kami senang karena makanannya enak sekali.
rows.note: end: how it was · 47 words in all

blocks.text: **Don't slip back into the present.** Indonesian stories use the same verb all the way (*kami pergi, kami berenang*), so learners often start in the past and then switch: *We went to the beach. We swim in the sea.* Check every verb before you send: *went, had, took, bought, was/were*. Words like *first, then, after that* and *so* also help to tell a story; you'll learn them in a later lesson. For now, time words with **and, but, because** are enough.

id.text: **Jangan kembali ke bentuk present.** Cerita dalam bahasa Indonesia memakai kata kerja yang sama dari awal sampai akhir (*kami pergi, kami berenang*), jadi pelajar sering mulai dengan bentuk lampau lalu berganti: *We went to the beach. We swim in the sea.* Periksa setiap kata kerja sebelum mengirim: *went, had, took, bought, was/were*. Kata seperti *first, then, after that* dan *so* juga membantu bercerita; kamu akan mempelajarinya di pelajaran berikutnya. Untuk sekarang, kata waktu dengan **and, but, because** sudah cukup.

blocks.prompt: Rina wrote: 'Last Sunday I went to the market and I buy some vegetables.' What's wrong?
blocks.explain: Last Sunday is the past, so every verb is past: went and bought. 'buy' slips back into the present. (bought, with ou, is the past of buy; brought is the past of bring.)

id.prompt: Rina menulis: 'Last Sunday I went to the market and I buy some vegetables.' Apa yang salah?
id.explain: Last Sunday itu masa lalu, jadi semua kata kerjanya lampau: went dan bought. 'buy' kembali ke bentuk present. (bought, dengan ou, adalah lampau dari buy; brought adalah lampau dari bring.)

resources.title: A message to a new friend (A2 reading)
resources.note: A friendly direct message with news and questions, starting 'Hi Lucia' and ending 'Bye for now'. Read it as a model, then do the exercises. Some sentences use tenses you haven't learnt yet (I have never seen…); just notice how he gives news and asks back.

id.note: Pesan langsung yang ramah berisi kabar dan pertanyaan, dimulai dengan 'Hi Lucia' dan ditutup dengan 'Bye for now'. Baca sebagai contoh, lalu kerjakan latihannya. Beberapa kalimat memakai tenses yang belum kamu pelajari (I have never seen…); cukup perhatikan cara dia memberi kabar dan bertanya balik.

resources.title: My last holiday (A2 writing)
resources.note: A model story about a trip in the past simple, with writing tips and exercises. It's longer than yours (about 190 words) and uses 'so' and a few tenses from later lessons: use it for ideas, and keep your story to 35–50 words.

id.note: Contoh cerita tentang perjalanan dengan past simple, dengan tips menulis dan latihan. Ceritanya lebih panjang dari ceritamu (sekitar 190 kata) dan memakai 'so' serta beberapa tenses dari pelajaran berikutnya: pakai untuk mencari ide, dan buat ceritamu tetap 35–50 kata.

id.intro: Selamat datang! Hari ini kamu menulis pesan singkat yang kamu kirim setiap hari: pesan WhatsApp atau email untuk teman berisi kabarmu dan sebuah pertanyaan, dan pesan sopan untuk atasanmu. Di akhir, kamu menulis cerita pendek tentang akhir pekanmu dalam 35–50 kata, dengan bentuk lampau yang sudah kamu kenal.
suggestedQuestions: Boleh tidak memakai emoji dan 'btw' di pesan bahasa Inggris?
Kenapa ditulis 'Did you go' dan bukan 'Did you went'?
Bagaimana cara menghitung kata dalam ceritaku?

assessment.sm-1: Kamu menulis email untuk manajermu, Bu Ani. Tulis ungkapan penutup yang sopan dalam bahasa Inggris, untuk diletakkan sebelum namamu.
assessment.sm-2: Manajermu, Pak Hasan, membantumu mengerjakan laporan. Tulis ucapan terima kasih yang sopan dalam bahasa Inggris untuk emailmu kepadanya (bukan 'Thanks!').
assessment.sm-3: Pakai catatan ini untuk menulis kabarmu dalam satu kalimat bahasa Inggris: I / buy / a new motorbike / last week
assessment.sm-4: Perbaiki kesalahan dalam kabar ini: Guess what? Last week we move to a new flat!
assessment.sm-5: Sari menulis: 'I was in Lombok last week!' Tanyakan balik tentang makanannya dalam bahasa Inggris. Pakai catatan ini: what / you / eat
assessment.sm-6: Kalimat ini dari cerita tentang akhir pekan lalu. Tulis dalam bentuk lampau: On Sunday we go to the market and buy some fruit.
assessment.sm-7: Gabungkan dua kalimat ini dengan because: We were very tired. We walked for five hours.
